title: Punctured generalization neighborhoods are spectral and lose one dimension
statement: Let $X$ be a spectral topological space [def-weil-spectral-space], let $n\geq1$ be an integer, and suppose $\dim X\leq n$ for topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $Z\subseteq X$ be closed and assume $X\setminus Z$ is quasi-compact. Define $W=\{x\in X:\overline{\{x\}}\cap Z\ne\varnothing\}$ and $S=W\setminus Z$, both with their subspace topologies. Then $S$ is spectral and $\dim S\leq n-1$. The assertions include $Z=\varnothing$, $Z=X$, and $X=\varnothing$, with $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$.

source.place: Tag 0AP0, lemma-make-spectral-space-minus; the dimension estimate is the specialization-chain argument in cohomology.tex, Tag 0A3G, proposition-cohomological-dimension-spectral, induction step proving (2).

proof.text: Put $U=X\setminus Z$. The closed subset $Z$ is quasi-compact: extend any open cover of $Z$ by $U$ to a cover of the quasi-compact space $X$, and take a finite subcover. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-generalizations-of-quasi-compact] with $E=Z$. It gives $W=\bigcap_{N\in I}N$, where $I$ is the set of all quasi-compact open neighborhoods $N$ of $Z$. Order $I$ by reverse inclusion. It is nonempty because $X\in I$; it is directed because $N\cap M\in I$ by quasi-separatedness in [def-weil-spectral-space]. Consequently $S=\bigcap_{N\in I}(N\cap U)$.

source.place: Tag 0A31, lemma-make-spectral-space, (3) implies (4); Tag 0AP0, lemma-make-spectral-space-minus, neighborhood construction

proof.text: Set $X_N=N\cap U$. It is quasi-compact open in $X$, since $N,U$ are quasi-compact open. Check spectrality directly from [def-weil-spectral-space]. The quasi-compact opens of $X_N$ are exactly the quasi-compact ambient opens contained in $X_N$: openness is transitive for open subspaces, and the subspace topology preserves quasi-compactness of a subset. Thus the ambient basis and finite-intersection property restrict to $X_N$. For sobriety, let $C$ be nonempty irreducible closed in $X_N$. Its ambient closure $D$ is irreducible: if $D\subseteq A\cup B$ for ambient closed $A,B$, irreducibility of $C$ puts $C$, and hence $D$, in one of them. Let $\eta$ be the unique generic point of $D$ in $X$. The open $X_N$ meets $D=\overline{\{\eta\}}$, so contains $\eta$; then $C=X_N\cap D=\overline{\{\eta\}}^{X_N}$. A second generic point of $C$ would also be generic for $D$, proving uniqueness. This proves spectrality of $X_N$. For $M\subseteq N$, the inclusion $X_M\hookrightarrow X_N$ is spectral: a quasi-compact open $B$ of $X_N$ is ambient quasi-compact open, so its inverse image $B\cap X_M$ is quasi-compact by quasi-separatedness of $X$.

source.place: Tag 0902, lemma-spectral-sub, quasi-compact-open case, and definition Tag 08YG; direct verification

proof.text: Use the inclusion maps $X_M\hookrightarrow X_N$ for $M\subseteq N$; identity and composition hold as identities of inclusions. The inclusions $p_N:S\hookrightarrow X_N$ exhibit $S$ as their topological limit. Indeed any compatible tuple consists of one ambient point: given $M,N$, compare both coordinates with the coordinate at $M\cap N$. Such a point lies in every $X_N$, hence in $S$ by step 1, and conversely a point of $S$ supplies a unique compatible tuple. All $p_N$ are continuous for the subspace topology. The coordinate at $N=X$ is the inclusion $S\hookrightarrow U$ and alone induces this topology, so the subspace topology is also the initial topology of all coordinates. The index is a set and is nonempty directed by step 1; all factors and transition maps are spectral by step 2. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-directed-limit-spectral] applies and proves that $S$ is spectral.

Consider any chain $C_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq C_m$ of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of $S$, as in [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Sobriety of $S$, proved in step 3 and defined in [def-weil-spectral-space], supplies generic points $\eta_i\in S$ with $C_i=\overline{\{\eta_i\}}^S$. Put $D_i=\overline{\{\eta_i\}}^X$. Each $D_i$ is nonempty irreducible closed: if it is covered by two closed sets, one contains $\eta_i$ and therefore all of $D_i$. The subspace closure identity gives $S\cap D_i=C_i$. Since $\eta_i\in C_{i+1}\subseteq D_{i+1}$, closedness gives $D_i\subseteq D_{i+1}$; equality would give $C_i=C_{i+1}$ on intersecting with $S$. We have therefore obtained a strict chain $D_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq D_m$ in $X$.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, proposition-cohomological-dimension-spectral, induction step for (2): expansion of the specialization-chain dimension estimate

proof.text: Because $\eta_0\in S\subseteq W$, there is $z\in Z\cap\overline{\{\eta_0\}}^X$. Put $D_{-1}=\overline{\{z\}}^X$. This is nonempty irreducible closed by the singleton argument of step 4. Since $D_0$ and $Z$ are closed and contain $z$, we have $D_{-1}\subseteq D_0\cap Z$. This inclusion in $D_0$ is strict, because $\eta_0\in D_0$ but $\eta_0\notin Z$. Thus $D_{-1}\subsetneq D_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq D_m$ has length $m+1$. The definition [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and $\dim X\le n$ give $m+1\le n$, hence $m\le n-1$. Every chain in $S$ has this bound, so $\dim S\le n-1$. If there are no chains, the same bound holds because $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, proposition-cohomological-dimension-spectral, induction step proving (2), dimension drop by appending a specialization in Z

proof.text: For $Z=\varnothing$ we have $W=\varnothing$ and $S=\varnothing$. For $Z=X$, reflexivity of closure gives $W=X$ and again $S=\varnothing$. If $X=\varnothing$ then also $S=\varnothing$. These cases are already covered by the nonempty directed system above (the index still contains $X$, even when it is empty); no step required a point of $S$ except when testing a nonempty chain. The empty space satisfies all four spectral conditions vacuously, and its dimension is $-\infty$ by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NL-8dbbe1664 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Proof-only split of an unchanged statement (stmt_deps unchanged, no new nodes, no re-split note in coord). I read all six steps in full and found no faults. (1) Z is closed in quasi-compact X, so it is quasi-compact. lem-weil-pbc-spectral-generalizations-of-quasi-compact with E=Z gives W as the intersection of the quasi-compact open neighbourhoods N of Z. These N form a nonempty directed set: X belongs to it and quasi-separatedness closes it under intersection. (2) Each N∩U is quasi-compact open and spectral, checked directly: it inherits the basis and quasi-separatedness, and it is sober because generic points of ambient closures lie in the open. The inclusions between them are spectral maps. (3) S is the limit of the N∩U: a compatible tuple is a single point of S, and the coordinate at N=X already induces the subspace topology. All hypotheses of lem-weil-pbc-spectral-directed-limit-spectral hold, so S is spectral. (4)-(5) A chain in S lifts to a strict chain of closures in X. Appending cl{z} for some z in Z∩cl{η_0} makes it strictly longer by one, because η_0 is not in Z. Hence dim S ≤ n−1. (6) The empty cases are correct. Sources match: topology.tex 0A31 (5004ff), 0AP0 (5068ff, the closed-constructible case, proved directly in step 2 without citing 0902), 0A2Z; cohomology.tex 0A3G induction step (2). No SGA. Small cases: the three-point chain η→y→z with Z={z} gives dim S=1 against dim X=2, so the bound is sharp; Spec of a DVR with n=1 gives dim S=0. No duplicate: the punctured cohomology-colimit node and the closed-subspace node state different results. I accept both tool_uses, which are generic spectral-space topology.
